title: legalContext — x402 extension info
description: The `info` payload of the `legalContext` x402 extension at challenge time: a Legal Context Protocol reference to the terms governing this transaction, plus the URL the terms document can be fetched from. The reference identifies the exact terms document; it is not the terms. This describes a technology harness and asserts nothing about whether any agreement is lawful, sound or enforceable.

type.description: The digest algorithm over the terms document. `sha256` is the only value this version defines.

value.description: The atrHash — SHA-256 of the terms document, lowercase hex with an 0x prefix.

legalContextUrl.description: Where the terms document this hash covers can be fetched. A reader verifies the document against `value`; the URL is a locator and never the authority.

receipt.title: legalContext — settlement-time info
receipt.$comment: WHY TWO DEFINITIONS IN ONE DOCUMENT: x402 §5.1.2 makes `schema` required and says it is the 'JSON Schema defining the expected structure of `info`', and the receipt-time `info` is not the challenge-time `info` — it carries three more fields. One pointer cannot define both shapes, so whichever block shared it would ship a `schema` that misdescribes its own `info`. A buyer still resolves ONE agreement's schema, which is why they stay in one document. WHY THE ROOT CARRIES NO $ref INDIRECTION: the root doubles as the INLINED wire schema — x402's Bazaar extension forbids external $ref/$id in an untrusted `schema` and the published placement inlines the root verbatim (minus $id and $defs), an equality the conformance suite gates — so the atrHash pattern is stated inline in both definitions rather than shared through a $defs pointer the wire copy would have to rewrite.
receipt.description: The same reference the 402 challenge carried, restated on the settlement response so the buyer holds an execution-time record of the terms actually in force when the payment landed — not only the ones proposed. The three extra fields exist to stop it being mistaken for a binding artifact, and they say the uncomfortable part out loud rather than omitting it.

phase.description: WHEN this reference was recorded: at settlement, i.e. the terms in force at execution time.

signatureCoverage.description: What signs this block: NOTHING, and it is carried in the clear. x402's only server-signed artifacts are the EIP-712 Offer and Receipt, which are closed types whose alteration the extension itself declares a breaking change, and whose signature covers the payload object rather than the surrounding envelope's `extensions` map. `none` is the truth on the wire.

weldCarrier.description: Where the BINDING actually lives. This block RESTATES the weld and never establishes it — on x402/EVM the record is bound by the EIP-3009 authorization nonce, which the payer signed.
